Anna (eng-platform): quick question — for the autofallback rollout: are we comfortable triggering a soft-degrade at a 5% error spike over a 1m window? :thinking:
Raj (eng-runtime): 5% feels tight for noisy endpoints. I'd prefer a smoothed metric (exponential decay) + a hysteresis window. e.g., detect >5% over 1m, require persistent >5% for 3m before 50% soft-degrade.
Anna (eng-platform): ok, that matches my gut. we also need a clear operator override and a way to see "why" in the console.
Maya (product): important — product needs the "why" reasons to surface: timeout, model OOM, high 5xx rate, latency tail. Can we standardize reason codes?
Raj (eng-runtime): yes. propose reason codes: TIMEOUT, OOM, KERNEL_ERR, KVS_MISS_RATE, RATE_LIMITED. We'll attach reason + sample rate to each decision.
Liu (eng-sre): telemetry note — we must emit a decision_id and trace_id for every routing decision (even sampled) so postmortem can replay. Also retention for these decision traces needs product/ops buy-in (storage cost).
Maya (product): agreed on decision_id. For UI, we want a compact "decision card" per event: time, reason, affected route, snapshot of metrics when triggered.
Anna (eng-platform): what about quota interplay? If we fallback to an cheaper model, does the request still count against dedicated capacity quotas?
Raj (eng-runtime): currently quotas are per-route. Two options: (A) count against original route (so cost/usage visible to owner), (B) count against fallback route (keeps accounting aligned with actual infra). I prefer A for billing clarity, but B helps capacity owners see load.
Maya (product): billing clarity is more important for customers. Maybe show both: increment original route usage and tag fallback route with a "served_as" metric.
Liu (eng-sre): we also need alerts not to escalate if upstream is flapping — add dampening and an oscillation guard to avoid flip-flop.
Raj (eng-runtime): agree. propose a two-stage policy: soft-degrade (sample X% of traffic) -> escalate to hard-degrade (100%) after N sustained windows. Soft-degrade should be sampled so we can validate quality regressions before full switch.
Anna (eng-platform): can you sketch a policy blob we can use for the console editor?
Raj (eng-runtime): sure — rough example: ```json
{
  "policy_name": "autofallback_v1",
  "triggers": [
    {"metric": "error_rate", "window_s": 60, "threshold_pct": 5},
    {"metric": "p99_latency_ms", "window_s": 60, "threshold_ms": 2000}
  ],
  "stages": [
    {"name": "soft", "sample_pct": 50, "min_duration_s": 180, "reason_codes": ["TIMEOUT","OOM","KERNEL_ERR"]},
    {"name": "hard", "sample_pct": 100, "min_duration_s": 600}
  ],
  "hysteresis": {"cooldown_s": 300, "oscillation_guard": true},
  "audit": {"emit_decision_ids": true, "log_fields": ["route","reason","sample_pct","backoff_counter"]}
}
```
Anna (eng-platform): perfect — that looks good for the editor. two UI asks: 1) a compact preview simulation mode (simulate on 10k reqs) and 2) an explainability tooltip for each reason code.
Maya (product): also need a safety toggle: "require operator approval before hard-degrade". Many enterprise customers will want a manual gate.
Raj (eng-runtime): add an operator_override flag and an audit trail entry for approvals. We can attach operator_id + timestamp.
Liu (eng-sre): on telemetry retention — let's default to sampling 100% for soft-degrades and 10% for routine decisions. Keep full traces for escalations and operator overrides. Ops cost estimates needed.
Anna (eng-platform): OpsBot — can you run a quick sim on the sample workload (10k reqs) and show expected cost change and false-positive risk?
OpsBot: simulation started: workload=10000 reqs, baseline=model-A, fallback=model-B (quantized).
OpsBot: simulation result: cost_delta=-17.8%, latency_p99_increase=+12ms, quality_sample_loss_est=0.9% (95% CI). flagged 42 decisions as "marginal".
Anna (eng-platform): good data. 0.9% quality loss seems acceptable if we can monitor examples.
Maya (product): UX idea — after soft-degrade start, surface a small "quality sampling" panel that shows sampled request/response diffs with an accept/reject button for operators. :eyes:
Raj (eng-runtime): we'll need an automated diff pipeline + differential eval hook. I can add a webhook sink for sampled pairs.
Liu (eng-sre): ops-level alerting: fire a P1 if hard-degrade engages for >10m across >3 routes. Otherwise page only for ops overrides or OOM clusters.
Anna (eng-platform): sounds like next steps: (1) Raj drafts policy schema and implement oscillation guard, (2) Raj + Liu estimate telemetry costs for full-trace retention, (3) Maya designs decision card + manual gate UX, (4) DevEx adds simulation button to console. I'll make tickets.
Maya (product): thumbs up. I'll sketch the decision card tomorrow.
Raj (eng-runtime): I'll post a PR with schema and a small simulator, ETA EOD Thurs.
Liu (eng-sre): I'll run cost estimates once schema final.
Anna (eng-platform): thanks everyone. merging this into our rollout doc and will ping for reviews. :thumbsup:
